correctness.rationale: Direct dot products give 24 adjacent pairs, eight adjacent triples, and no adjacent quadruple. Up to t=π/4 a nonadjacent pair intersects only at a possible null contact at the endpoint. Pair onset is half the adjacent separation; summing the three cap inequalities proves triple onset at arccos√(2/3), attained at the normalized sum of the three sites. On a cap circle the allowable azimuth intervals have half-width β, and in a clique the other center bearings differ by η. Their intersection has length 2β−η when positive. The boundary curvatures are cot(t), the corner turns are γ, and Gauss–Bonnet gives L and T as stated. Cross-check without inclusion–exclusion: in the cell of (1,1,0)/√2, polar azimuth φ from (1,−1,0)/√2 toward (0,0,1) gives radial boundary arctan[1/(|cos φ|+√2|sin φ|)]. In a quadrant this denominator is √3 cos(φ−d), d=arctan√2. Its levels give a,b,c, and differentiating the area below t gives F′=(12/π) sin t [π/2−2β+(β−η/2)_+] for a<t<c; below a the bracket is π/2. This equals the derivative of the frozen formula because L′=4β sin t and T′=3(2β−η)sin t when active. At b, β=η/2 and β′=3, so integration yields T=3√3 ε²+O(ε³). At c, β=d, β′=√2, β″=−3√2. Thus F′(c−ε)=(12/π)(ε+ε²/2+O(ε³)), which gives both stated survival coefficients. Equality at the covering endpoint occurs only at the six signed axes; distance level sets have area zero. Frozen verification and checker were inspected, not executed.
